name: Will Combining Seismic Retrofits with Renovations Trigger Reassessment in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: Can a seismic retrofit in Los Angeles County trigger a full property tax reassessment if it is combined with other building improvements?
mainEntity.text: Can a seismic retrofit in Los Angeles County trigger a full property tax reassessment if it is combined with other building improvements?

acceptedAnswer.text: California law allows many seismic retrofit improvements to be excluded from property tax reassessment, but that protection is not blanket coverage for all construction performed at the same time. When a Los Angeles County owner bundles a retrofit with major upgrades—such as full interior remodels, new stories, extensive tenant improvements, or system overhauls—the Assessor can separate the project into exempt seismic components and taxable non-seismic new construction. In practice, the seismic anchorage, strengthening, and hazard mitigation measures typically qualify for exclusion, while unrelated improvements may be added to the property’s assessed value. The risk of a substantial reassessment increases when owners use the retrofit as an opportunity for large value-adding renovations. To manage this, owners should work with their contractor and design team to clearly segregate costs and scopes of work: one set of line items for seismic retrofit elements and another for non-seismic improvements. This detail should carry through the plans, permits, and invoices so that the County Assessor can easily identify what qualifies. Filing the seismic exclusion claim form on time and supplying detailed documentation allows officials to exempt the eligible portion while assessing the rest. Discussing your plans with a knowledgeable tax professional or assessor’s office staff before construction can help you understand the likely tax impact and structure the project to avoid unexpected reassessment.
acceptedAnswer.description: Seismic retrofits alone can qualify for California’s property tax exclusion, but combining them with broader renovations may trigger reassessment on the non-seismic portion. If structural work is bundled with substantial upgrades, the Assessor can treat those added improvements as taxable new construction while exempting qualifying seismic work.
